text.p: Bonds closed firmer, taking their cue from Spain, but the cash market slightly underperformed its neighbour due to a lack of players.

Dealers said this lack of sparkle from Portugal leaves room for the market to outperform on Monday when the spread could widen back out to around 10 basis points for the benchmark 10-year bonds. Providing, of course, liquidity improves.
Futures however closed at their day's highs, keeping close to the Spanish trend.
"Monday should see fresh gains," said one trader referring to Europe's so-called 'peripheral' bond markets, principally Spain and Italy.
Traders said that the higher than expected U.S. farm payroll figures had triggered short-covering in U.S. Treasuries after an initial sharp fall and this had driven Europe higher.
"In Spain, the movement was amplified by rumours of a rate cut," added another trader.
